deviations_from_plan: STEP 3's INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. The plan said to rewrite the isolation rationale 'because the stated reason is measured FALSE'. The claim has two halves with different truth values: the antecedent HOLDS (a fresh unconstrained resolve really does take sklearn 1.9.1 -- a new venv got it) while the CONSEQUENCE is refuted (1.8.0 already satisfies the package, so a project-env install moves nothing). An earlier pass of mine called the whole premise REFUTED, over-correcting in the other direction. Both docstrings now carry the three-way decomposition instead of either blunt verdict.

STEP 3 FIXED THE PROBE rather than only re-emitting its record, which is more than the plan asked. Re-emitting would have shipped an artifact already known wrong in two ways: it reported the environment ABSENT while a working interpreter existed on C: (a FALSE absence -- the same defect fixed in find_inputs the same day, which searched only drive roots while the substrate sat repo-local), and its isolation_claim.status asserted a bare REFUTED. Verdict vocabulary untouched: ENV_ABSENT is scoped to the DOCUMENTED path and is correct about it.

STEP 1 DID NOT REUSE require_external_dir LITERALLY, because the plan's Reusable-Code Survey item 1 does not fit stage A. resolve_external_root reports `configured` only when the path ALREADY is a directory, which is right for an INPUT root and wrong for stage A's OUTPUT dir -- on a first export the leaf legitimately does not exist, so the resolver would refuse a good run. Stage A checks the nearest existing ANCESTOR instead. Stages A and C therefore do NOT share a helper; that is a finding, not laziness.

STEP 1 FOR STAGE B WAS DEFERRED WITHIN THE RUN and done under a paused supervisor. Stage B's module was live under the running Pool. Pool() carries no maxtasksperchild so the 7 children never re-import, making the edit safe for the running job -- but a watchdog relaunch WOULD pick up new code, so the watchdog was stopped for the ~6 minute edit window and restored only after the edit was verified (parses, stdlib-only, no dna_decode at any depth, reachable path returns, a real 3-tile decomposition with 0 errors, 25 tests green). Both pause and resume are logged in data/promcalc/watchdog.log.

out_of_plan_work_this_run.what: hardened the watchdog with stall detection (review issues 4 and 5)
out_of_plan_work_this_run.why_not_a_plan_step: the watchdog is instrumentation this session built around Step 5, not a step the plan defines. Recorded here because it changes how Step 5 behaves unattended.
out_of_plan_work_this_run.issue_4_hang_detection: liveness alone could not tell healthy from hung, so '7 processes alive, zero tiles completing' would have waited forever and lost the night. Now the total size across the main file and all shards must GROW between polls; 20 min flat while alive is treated as dead.
out_of_plan_work_this_run.issue_5_subsumed_not_fixed_as_stated: the review proposed tightening the over-broad liveness match to the run-lock's PID. That would have been WORSE: on 2026-10-22 killing the parent left six workers at 100% CPU with the lock PID already dead, so a PID-only check would have read 'dead', relaunched, and run a second job beside the orphans. The broad match is fail-safe toward 'alive' and is CORRECT provided progress is monitored -- which issue 4's fix now does. Kept broad, deliberately.
out_of_plan_work_this_run.no_kill_on_stall: because the liveness match is over-broad, an automated kill could take down an unrelated multiprocessing job. The relaunch is guarded by the run-lock's own PID-liveness check instead, so the safe outcome is reached without this script choosing what to kill.
out_of_plan_work_this_run.verified: parse-clean; the progress signal GROWS on the live job (321,220 bytes in 75 s, so a healthy run cannot false-stall); the stall predicate exercised three ways including the positive case (flat and older than the threshold -> STALL).
